label: PF Backlog 642
title: Process: Gate 0 + human-only decisions + Gate 2.5 convergence/scope guard (BI-PF-1471)
body: Make the five enterprise operating rules enforced: Gate 0 reconciliation/impact table, human-only decisions with risk acceptance, one review per sha, SCOPE findings non-blocking with follow-up, and the table visible in precheck.

brief.problem: Make the five enterprise operating rules enforced: Gate 0 reconciliation/impact table, human-only decisions with risk acceptance, one review per sha, SCOPE findings non-blocking with follow-up, and the table visible in precheck.
brief.what_adds: Process: Gate 0 + human-only decisions + Gate 2.5 convergence/scope guard (BI-PF-1471)
brief.why: Make the five enterprise operating rules enforced: Gate 0 reconciliation/impact table, human-only decisions with risk acceptance, one review per sha, SCOPE findings non-blocking with follow-up, and the table visible in precheck.

objective: Enforce Gate 0 + human-only Gate 1/2 + Gate 2.5 convergence/scope rules.
acceptance_criteria: Gate 0 check: an item entering new->in_progress must carry a non-empty reconciliation block (prior_decisions, existing_path, assumptions, divergences, open_questions) and an impact-review table (claim/verdict/evidence/recommendation incl. API and AC rows) plus language and api_impact decisions; precheck fails otherwise.

Gate 1/2 decisions are human-only: gate_decide requires --hil-confirmed (recorded in the decision), validates accepted_risks {owner, until, rationale}, refuses in CI, and approval treats SCOPE findings as resolved only with a follow-up item.
Gate 2.5 convergence: a second review for the same item+sha is refused unless --rereview; one review per immutable sha; re-review only after code changes.
Gate 2.5 scope guard: findings dispositioned SCOPE are non-blocking and must reference a follow-up item; new functional scope cannot block the approved delivery.
Operational visibility: gate0_check prints the reconciliation and impact-review table in precheck output; gate-brief renders the same for HIL.
Tests: gate0 negative/positive, SCOPE resolution, accepted-risk validation, duplicate-review refusal; precheck PASS.
in_scope: Process: Gate 0 + human-only decisions + Gate 2.5 convergence/scope guard (BI-PF-1471)
approach: Process: Gate 0 + human-only decisions + Gate 2.5 convergence/scope guard (BI-PF-1471)

assumptions: SCOPE findings belong to a new backlog item

impact_review.claim: Gate 0 is a new precheck gate, not a duplicate of DoD
Human decisions use existing decision ledger
SCOPE findings are non-blocking but traceable

verification: Objective achieved: Process: Gate 0 + human-only decisions + Gate 2.5 convergence/scope guard (BI-PF-1471)

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend existing gate/guardrail owners: `core/design_guardrails.py` (checklist enforcement at stage=diff), `core/guardrails.py` + `core/run_guard.py` (rule registry, single-writer per rule per CL-001), `config/guardrail-policy.json` + `config/gate-baseline.json` (declare the five rules), and `/api/v1/engineering/gates` + `/api/v1/engineering/pidl/decisions` (Gate 0 reconciliation/impact table, human-only decision records with risk acceptance, one-review-per-sha convergence). Add SCOPE findings as non-blocking disposition class surfaced by precheck (reuse BI-PF-1430 pattern: store on item + gate sheet).
conflict_findings: BI-PF-1430 touches gate-surface storage — coordinate field ownership
No concurrent task owns guardrail-policy.json rule registry
duplication_findings: BI-PF-1430 already surfaces 1.5/2.5 findings on item+gate sheet — extend, not rebuild
BI-PF-0335 covers contract reconciliation artifact/Gate 0 — hook into it for the impact table
BI-0205 defines PR pre-check gates — precheck visibility belongs there
CL-006 already enforces Gate 1 finding embedding; this item generalizes to all five rules
analysis.rationale: All five rules have existing owners (guardrails, decisions API, gate sheet, precheck); work is configuration + policy enforcement + one new table surface, mostly reuse with low drift.
assumptions: Existing gate sheet/guardrail-policy are the canonical config surfaces
One-review-per-sha can be derived from existing run/sha metadata
Human risk-acceptance is recorded via pidl/decisions outcome endpoint
risks: Rule overlap with existing gates may double-report findings
Human-only decision path could block automation if mis-gated
Precheck surface regression if precheck schema changes
missing_info: Which of the five rules are BLOCKING vs WARN at first rollout
Who is the accountable human approver role per tenant for risk acceptance
Whether SCOPE follow-ups create backlog items automatically or via manual link
